problem.para: In the body of the Working Draft, there occasionally appears a point that requires particular attention, highlighted thus:
An SQL predicate named GRAPH_EXISTS has been proposed, to test whether a pattern is satisfied in a property graph.
An SQL value expression named GRAPH_VALUE has been proposed, to extract a value from a property graph.
It may be desirable for GRAPH_TABLE to support multiple input graphs.
Convenience syntax may be provided for edge tables that model a 1:n relationship through a foreign key in a vertex table to another vertex table or itself.

Path pattern union is not defined using left recursion. SXM-052 believed that it should be possible to support left recursion but declined to do so for expediency. It is a Language Opportunity to support left recursion.
Linked to .

As WG3:MMX-026 has shown, there is currently no need to add a keyword before the in a . However, in the future it may become necessary to add such a keyword to allow for multiple s and MATCH clauses within the same (and/or to align with GQL). The exact keyword has yet to be determined. Examples include (but are not limited to) FROM, ON, USE, and WITHIN.
It has been proposed that a macro name may be a in a .
Linked to .
It may be possible to permit nested quantifiers. WG3:W01-014 contained a discussion of a way to support aggregates at different depths of aggregation if there are nested quantifiers.
Linked to .

It may be possible to enforce implicit joins of unconditional singletons exposed by a as part of the GRs for . This was discussed in a SQL/PG ad hoc meeting on September 8, 2020. It was decided not to attempt that change as part of WG3:W04-009R1, leaving it as a future possibility.
Linked to .

It has been suggested that it might be possible to treat the specified in as merely providing a default rather than a mandatory one for each . Whereas nested is prohibited, this may be a feasible avenue of growth. On the other hand, perhaps a less definitive verb than KEEP may be appropriate when specifying a default .
Linked to .
It has been proposed that unconditional singletons exposed by prior MATCH clauses may also be joined implicitly.
Was linked to <ExtPPref ref="PPgql059" standard="39075"/>.

WG3:W04-009R1 recognized that a graph query may have a sequence of MATCH clauses, with the bindings of one MATCH clause visible in all subsequent MATCH clauses in the same invocation of , and that it should be permissible to reference such variables in any simply contained in a subsequent MATCH clause.
See also .
The equivalent LO in GQL, GQL-051, was resolved by WG3:GYD-031.
The ability to specify cheapest queries (analogous to SHORTEST, but minimizing the sum of costs along a path) is desirable.
Linked to .

In addition to SHORTEST GROUP, it has been proposed to support SHORTEST [ k ] WITH TIES, with the semantics to return the first k matches (where k defaults to 1) when sorting matches in ascending order on number of edges, and also return any matches that have the same number of edges as the last of the k matches. This is the semantics of WITH TIES in .
Linked to .
WG3:W04-009R1 believed it should be possible to support nested selectors using recursion, but did not undertake that. It is a Language Opportunity to support nested selectors.
Linked to .

WG3:W04-009R1 believed it should be possible to support selectors within quantifiers with a finite upper bound, but did not undertake that. (This comment applies to a static upper bound, not dynamic, since we are forbidding multiple selectors within a restrictor.) It is a Language Opportunity to support selectors within quantifiers with a finite upper bound.
Linked to .

With more work, it is possible to recognize when a vertex variable is declared uniformly in the first or the last position in every operand of a . However, WG3:W04-009R1 declined to make the effort because it is easy for the user to factor out such a vertex pattern. For example, instead of
the user can write
Thus a more general definition of right or left boundary variable is possible.
Linked to .

WG3:W08-018 prohibited a selector contained in a or PU, but believed that if PU is at the top of a path pattern, and a selector is at the top of an operand of PU, then this scenario does not violate compositionality. It is a Language Opportunity to permit this scenario.
Linked to .

In the BNF for , the delimiter tokens <~[ ]~> have been suggested as a synonym for -[ ]-. The synonym for the - () would then be <~>, the synonym for would use the delimiter tokens <~/ /~> and the synonym for would use the tokens <~ and > surrounding a label as originally proposed in WG3:MMX-060. These synonyms might be considered to make the table of edge patterns more harmonious and internally consistent.
Linked to .

problem.para: During the discussion of WG3:W09-010 Disallow mixed property types, it was noted that it could be beneficial to PGQ users to relax the restriction imposed by WG3:W09-010 that all properties with the same name within a given graph must have the same data type. Any approach to allow mixed property types needs to address the problems with doing so as outlined in WG3:W09-010. Note that the effect of WG3:W09-010 was replaced by W09-034 but the comment still applies.

The bindings of a group reference flatten nested lists. This may be acceptable for SQL aggregates, which have no support for nested groupings, but may be inadequate to fully capture the semantics of a group reference in a graph pattern. MMX-035r2 section 4.1 Desynchronized lists pointed out a problem with reducing group variables to lists: two lists may be interleaved, but the reduction to separate lists can lose this information. The example given is
A solution may find matches to A and B in any order. With separate lists of matches of A and B, it will not be easy to reconstruct the precise sequence of interleaved matches to A and B.
A similar problem can arise with nested quantifiers. MMX-035r2 section 4.2 Nested quantifiers gives this example:

With this pattern, there can be 0 or more bindings to B between any two consecutive bindings to C1 and C2. With just independent lists of matches to C1, B and C2, it will not be easy to determine which bindings to B lie between which bindings to C1 and C2.
Linked to .
Syntax Rules and Conformance Rules regarding permissible s must be revisited if we permit a sequence of MATCH clauses.
See also .

The is expressed as a predicate about the vertex, while it is most often used to pose questions about the edge. If an alternative form of these predicates was available that put the edge as the first operand, this predicate would be more useful in combination with .
Linked to .
WG3:W20-030 only proposed support for graph aggregates with exactly one aggregated element reference. This leaves the following unsupported:
A possible work-around is a LET clause enabling the definition of properties of subpath variables, like this:
problem.code: MATCH TRAIL (P = (A) -> (B) LET AX = A.X, BX = B.X)+ WHERE CORR (P.AX, P.BX) > 0.5

problem.para: WG3:W20-030 acknowledged that support for aggregates of vertex variables is poor. For example, given the pattern

there is no element variable for all vertices: P references all but the last vertex, and Q references all but the first vertex. For certain aggregates such as SUM, AVG, MAX and MIN there is a work-around, to add one singleton vertex variable to the pattern to capture the vertex that is missed at one end of the quantified path pattern or the other. Thus
problem.code: MATCH TRAIL ((P) -> (Q))+ (PP) WHERE (CASE WHEN SUM(P.X) IS NOT NULL THEN SUM(P.X) ELSE 0) + (CASE WHEN PP.X IS NOT NULL THEN PP.X ELSE 0 END ) > 10
problem.para: tests whether the sum of property X on all vertices totals more than 10. However, this work-around does not help with percentiles, and is an ugly imposition on the user in any case.
RPR (row pattern recognition) has a notion of union variables which might be adapted to address this problem.
WG3:W07-014 discusses some approaches that might be followed if it is desired to permit non-local references to group element variables.
It may be possible to permit one GRAPH_TABLE nested within another to share an element variable, with implicit equijoin semantics.
WG3:W16-013 proposed concatenated MATCH to express lateral inner join.
WG3:W16-013 proposed OPTIONAL MATCH to express lateral left outer join.
WG3:W16-013 proposed EXISTS (MATCH ) as a predicate to test for the existence of a match.
It might be valuable to add an option to the (KEEP DISTINCT) to allow reducing to a set of distinct bindings to global singletons.
It is a Language Opportunity to support references to subpath variables, for example, in , or a TOTAL_COST function once CHEAPEST is defined.
Linked to .

The only use of is in , which WG3:RKE-031 limited to the COLUMNS clause in SQL/PGQ (see section 5.10 Predicates on PATH_LENGTH). It is a Language Opportunity to analyze predicates on PATH_LENGTH. Possibly restrictions might be added to , since they are likely to apply to any other scalar functions or predicates on .

GQL provides the ability to express a set of properties to be matched using equality semantics using a shorthand syntax derived from JSON object notation. Such syntax has been accepted into the draft GQL standard. In order to maintain syntactic compatibility between GQL and SQL/PGQ adding this syntax to SQL/PGQ should be considered as well.
It would be useful to be have a function to export an element binding, a path binding, or a multipath binding in JSON.

In addition to the ALTER PROPERTY GRAPH operations outlined in BNE-027r1, it it would be potentially useful to support an operation that modifies a single label that is implemented by more than one element table.

The definition of vertex says that it is a fundamental unit of which a property graph [] is formed. The same could be said of edges but that definition does not say so. Some alignment might be desirable.
Following the lead text of , talks about an empty path binding. It could also be noted here that a subpath binding may be empty.

Consider NO PARTITIONING semantics for selective path patterns, alongside the extant partition-by-endpoint semantics. In this would mean a way of finding the shortest path among all CANDIDATES, rather than within each PART. This discussion was last surfaced (albeit inconclusively) in WG3:MMX-059, and was recently referred to in passing in WG3:W07-013.

Regarding , YTZ-036 section 4.6.2 proposed WHERE FOR k REPS syntax to address the use case of expressing a condition that stretches over multiple repetitions of a . This addition should be considered.

The rules for patterns allowed within a may be unnecessarily strict. The Syntax Rules do not allow a to be contained within a . This is however equivalent to the containing a where one of the operands has a minimum path length of zero, which is allowed. The Syntax Rules could be changed according to Section 7.2 in [W07-009].

The rules for patterns allowed within a may be unnecessarily strict. The Syntax Rules do not allow another within a . This is essentially a no-op and therefore harmless. It is also possible to express the same semantics using a where one of the operands has a minimum path length of zero. The Syntax Rules further do not allow a within a . This is equivalent to an alternation between the in question and a pattern with a path length of zero. The Syntax Rules could be changed according to Section 7.2 in [W07-009].

From a schema evolution point-of-view, sometimes it might be better if the SELECT privilege on a property graph were not grantable, even if the user has all the right privileges in place for it to be grantable. An option on the CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH statement should be provided to allow for that possibility.
For the phrases LE shall identify a vertex label of PG and LE shall identify an edge label of PG, this document does not appear to provide a definition of vertex label or edge label.

and refer to formal semantics. It is not clear what formal semantics means. It does not mean the formal semantics as it would be meant conventionally in CS (denotational, operational, axiomatic). Perhaps the formal semantic refers to the stepwise presentation of the semantics specified in .
Linked to .
Pattern in is inconsistent with the text. The pattern ()-()-() cannot be matched in a graph ()~[]~(). The pattern ()-[]-() can be. Is that what was intended?
Linked to .

When a tabular property graph is converted to a pure property graph, the specification uses language like such that the value of the edge source key of ER is equal to the value of the source vertex key of SR. But it is not specified what collation applies to this equality operation.

solution.para: The collation for these equality operations should be derived via in SQL/Foundation.

problem.para: If the linkage between the edge table and the source/destination vertex tables is established via explicit key columns ( and ), then there are no requirements that the data types and collations (if applicable) of the corresponding key columns are compatible in a way that they can be compared for equality. In the alternative case that the linkage is provided by an existing foreign key, the requirements for foreign keys provide such restrictions.

solution.para: Add syntax rules that the data types and collations of the corresponding key columns need to match in the same way as they would for a foreign key definition.

problem.para: The declared type collation of properties is not specified.

solution.para: The declared type collation of a property of a particular label is derived from the definition of the property using the usual rules for deriving the collation of expressions.

problem.para: Functionality, if any, to support the Vector type needs to be provided.
